papers.title: Stationary bistable fronts on a periodic necklace graph: existence, stability and multiplicity
papers.abstract: We study stationary fronts for a bistable reaction-diffusion equation with the McKean reaction on a periodic necklace metric graph. For profiles that agree on each pair of parallel edges, the problem reduces to a scalar equation on the real line with a periodic, piecewise constant diffusion coefficient. The diffusion contrast of the necklace is not small, so the coefficient cannot be treated as a small perturbation of a constant. Because the McKean reaction is piecewise linear, the equation is affine between threshold crossings and coefficient interfaces, and a front is determined explicitly by its crossing points. We find an explicit interval of reaction thresholds, the pinning interval, such that stationary fronts, monotone or not, exist exactly for thresholds in this interval. Up to translations by the spatial period, there are exactly two decreasing fronts at each interior threshold and one front at each endpoint. For each fixed interior threshold, one decreasing front is Lyapunov stable and the other is unstable in the $W^{1,\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ norm, among mild solutions with one continuously moving threshold crossing. The crossing phases of the two decreasing fronts also determine nonmonotone fronts. For each interior threshold and odd $m\geq3$, choose $m$ periods of the coefficient that are sufficiently far apart. There are then exactly $2^m$ fronts with one threshold crossing in each chosen period and none elsewhere. Varying the chosen periods gives infinitely many inequivalent fronts with $m$ crossings.

papers.title: Semi-discrete approximation of Ma\~n\'e, Aubry and Mather sets
papers.abstract: We study a variational discretization in time of Aubry--Mather theory for Tonelli Lagrangians on the flat torus. We define discrete Ma\~n\'e, Aubry and Mather sets, establish their compactness and inclusion properties, and investigate their convergence as the time step tends to zero. We prove upper-limit results for the Ma\~n\'e sets and, when the continuous Aubry set has finitely many static classes, for the Aubry sets. We obtain full Kuratowski and Hausdorff convergence of the Aubry sets when this set is a single equilibrium or periodic orbit, and, under additional assumptions, a finite union of equilibria. Every weak limit of discrete Mather measures is a continuous Mather measure. For equilibrium Aubry sets, we give sufficient conditions for exact preservation of Mather sets and measure families at small time steps. A mechanical example illustrates these results and exhibits exact preservation of the Aubry set as well.

papers.title: Higher-order asymptotic formulae for periodic orbits of 3-dimensional volume-preserving Anosov flows and the Foulon conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $X^t$ be a volume-preserving Anosov flow of class $C^7$ on a closed $3$-manifold. We consider a sequence of periodic orbits which shadow a homoclinic loop of a fixed periodic orbit $\gamma$, and derive higher-order asymptotic expansions for their periods $T_n$ and for the logarithms of their unstable multipliers $\log\lambda_n$. We give geometric interpretations of the coefficients in these expansions, in particular in terms of the Anosov cocycle (\`a la Hurder-Katok) and the longitudinal Anosov cocycle (\`a la Foulon-Hasselblatt), evaluated on $\gamma$. Following the idea of De Simoi-Leguil-Vinhage-Yang, we compare these asymptotics when volume is the measure of maximal entropy. In this case, the equilibrium-state characterizations of volume and the measure of maximal entropy synchronize periods and exponents: $\log\lambda_n=hT_n$. Matching the coefficients of the two asymptotic expansions forces the cohomology classes of both cocycles to vanish. Then the work of Foulon-Hasselblatt on the longitudinal Anosov cocycle, together with Foulon's work on the contact case, yields the Foulon Conjecture for flows of class $C^7$: if volume is the measure of maximal entropy, then, up to a finite cover, $X^t$ is smoothly conjugate either to a constant-roof suspension of a hyperbolic automorphism of the $2$-torus or to a finite cover of the constant-speed geodesic flow on a closed hyperbolic surface.

papers.title: A generalization of Gordon's Theorem to arbitrary winding number
papers.abstract: We study minimizers of the Keplerian action functional with homogeneous potential of type $1/|u|^\alpha$ on periodic loops with fixed winding number $k \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}$. This extends the classical theorems of Gordon and Venturelli, closing the previously open case $\alpha \in (1,2)$, $|k|\geq 2$. We show that the $k$-circular solution loses local minimality below the threshold $\alpha = 2-1/|k|^2$, and that minimizers are collision-free above $\alpha = 2-1/|k|$. Combining these results with the existence of precessing periodic orbits in between, we obtain a full classification of the minimizer in terms of $\alpha$ and $k$, which we also verify numerically for $k=2$.

papers.title: Effective Multiplicative Ergodic Theorems for Banach Space Cocycles
papers.abstract: The multiplicative ergodic theorem (MET) describes the asymptotic growth rates of $q$-volumes under the iterates of an operator cocycle, i.e., compositions of operators driven by a stationary process, organizing the underlying space into equivariant filtrations or splittings into so called Oseledets subspaces. For operator cocycles in finite dimensions, and more generally in Hilbert spaces, one can control the geometry of the Oseledets subspaces given by the MET via the convergence rates of finite-time volume growth data. This makes the MET "effective" for matrix and Hilbert-space operator cocycles. We extend this effective theory to cocycles of Banach-space operators, obtaining quantitative angle estimates that are new even in the finite-dimensional setting. We take a sequential approach \`{a} la Raghunathan and Ruelle, allowing us to separate the geometric argument of the MET from measure-theoretic considerations. This permits weaker cocycle measurability hypotheses for the non-invertible and semi-invertible METs on a broad class of Banach spaces, including nonseparable ones. As an application, we establish the MET for transfer operator cocycles on $\operatorname{BV}[0,1]$ associated with jointly measurable random Lasota-Yorke maps.

papers.title: Flexibility of topological entropy and factor persistence in the $C^0$-Gromov Hausdorff topology
papers.abstract: We prove that every surjective topological dynamical system on a compact metric space can be approximated in the $C^0$-Gromov--Hausdorff topology by homeomorphisms with any prescribed topological entropy in $[0,+\infty]$, even when simultaneous approximation of its sets of invariant and ergodic measures is required. We also establish a rigidity result under uniform geometric bounds in a fixed dimension: for a homeomorphism of a closed, connected Riemannian manifold, topological stability in the sense of Gromov--Hausdorff guarantees its persistence as a factor of sufficiently close perturbations within the same geometric class. This persistence prevents topological entropy from decreasing and ensures that every invariant or ergodic measure of the original system admits a lift of the same type to the perturbed system.

papers.title: Spectrum of the basilica group and the associated real and complex 2D dynamics
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the iteration over the real and complex loci of a specific rational map, found by Grigorchuk and Zuk. This two dimensional map arises as the renormalization map which yields the density of states measure associated with the iterated monodromy group of the Basilica Julia set. It admits two natural complex currents, and we construct their real analogs and show that they are laminar. Finally, this yields some consequences on the properties of the density of states measures and its support.

papers.title: Global injectivity and real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the global injectivity of local diffeomorphisms in $\mathbb{R}^n$, extending the criterions of Braun and Llibre in [{\it Pacific J. Math.} {\bf 333} (2024) 1--15] from the planar radial case to arbitrary dimension. Then we extend the results of Llibre and Mello in [{\it Bull. Sci. Math.} {\bf 213} (2026) 103889] to arbitrary dimension, obtaining two necessary and sufficient conditions for the real Jacobian conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^n$ by qualitative theory of differential equations. Finally, using weighted Poincar\'e compactification in $\mathbb{R}^n$, we provide a sufficient condition for the real Jacobian conjecture.

papers.title: On the homeomorphism group of the Cantor set: monotone and measure preserving maps
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be the Cantor set, $G=\operatorname{Homeo}(E)$, let $P\le G$ be the group of order preserving homeomorphisms and $L\le G$ the group of homeomorphisms preserving the Cantor--Lebesgue measure $\lambda$. We study how $G$ is built from these two subgroups. In 2003, Glasner and Weiss stated that $G=LP=PL$. We show that this is not the case, in fact $PL$ and $LP$ are two different proper subsets of $G$. On the other hand, $PL$ is a dense $G_\delta$ subset of $G$, the multiplication map $P\times L\to PL$ is a homeomorphism, and $G=PLP=LPL$. In particular, every homeomorphism of $E$ is conjugate to an element of $PL$. We classify the double cosets $PgL$ using special clopen values set. There are continuum many of them, and $PL$ is the only one which is not meager. We prove that $G$ is topologically generated by one element of $P$ and one element of $L$ and these two generators produce the Thompson's group $V$. We also show that the generic homeomorphism of $E$ is the product of a generic element of $P$ and a generic element of $L$. The equality $G=PL$ fails also if $\lambda$ is replaced by any other full nonatomic measure.

papers.title: Partial rigidity and q-additive functions
papers.abstract: A system $(X,\mu, T)$ is partially rigid with constant $\delta>0$ if there exists an incresing sequence $(n_k)$ such that $\displaystyle \liminf_{k \to \infty } \mu(A \cap T^{-n_k}A) \geq \delta \mu(A)$ for every measurable $A \subset X$. The partial rigidity rate is the largest constant of partial rigidity. We characterize the partial rigidity rate of subshifts arising from $q$-additive functions $\pmod M$ in terms of quantities arising from B\'esineau's theorem. With this, we build a family of strongly $q$-additive functions to deduce that the collection of partial rigidity rates for substitution subshifts is dense in $[0,1]$ answering a question of Donoso, Maass and the author.

papers.title: The convergence-divergence criterion for the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma and Liv\v{s}ic theorem
papers.abstract: We establish a new dynamical convergence-divergence criterion for the existence of Lipschitz functions with continuous sub-actions, over general dynamical systems. This unifies and generalises various versions of the Ma\~n\'e cohomology lemma, in the setting of uniformly expanding maps, and systems with indifferent fixed points. One consequence is that for any compact metric space $(X,\rho)$, and Lipschitz Ruelle-expanding map $T:X\to X$, a metric transform $\omega$ satisfies Dini's criterion $\int_0 \omega(s)s^{-1}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if every function that is Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$ has a continuous sub-action. Another consequence is that if $T$ is an expanding circle map of Manneville-Pomeau type $\alpha\in(0,1)$, then $\omega$ satisfies the convergence criterion $\int_0 \omega(s)s^{-1-\alpha}\, ds <\infty$ if and only if every function that is Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$ has a continuous sub-action. For the latter class of maps $T$, with $\omega$ satisfying the convergence criterion, we prove a Liv\v{s}ic theorem for functions that are Lipschitz for $\omega\circ\rho$: if $\int f\, d\mu=0$ for all invariant measures $\mu$, then there exists a continuous function $\varphi$ such that $f=\varphi\circ T-\varphi$, where $\varphi$ is Lipschitz with respect to $D_\alpha(\omega)\circ\rho$, and $D_\alpha(\omega)(t)= \int_0^t \omega(s)s^{-1-\alpha} ds$.

papers.title: Marked length spectrum and area of surfaces with Anosov geodesic flow
papers.abstract: More than twenty years ago, Croke and Dairbekov showed that a negatively curved metric $g_0$ on a closed surface has minimal area among all negatively curved Riemannian metrics $g$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $g_0$. We show that the curvature assumption on the second metric can be removed and extend this result to reversible Finsler metrics. More precisely, we prove that a reversible Finsler metric $F_0$ on a closed surface whose geodesic flow is Anosov has minimal area among all reversible Finsler metrics $F$ on the same surface whose marked length spectrum is greater or equal to that of $F_0$.

papers.title: Energy Discontinuity of the Lyapunov Exponent for Quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger Operators with Gevrey Potentials
papers.abstract: We construct quasiperiodic Schr\"odinger operators with Gevrey potentials for which the Lyapunov exponent is discontinuous in the spectral energy. More precisely, let \(\alpha\in\R\setminus\mathbb Q\) satisfy the Diophantine condition \(\|k\alpha\|_{\T}\geq\gamma |k|^{-\tau}\) for all \(k\in\Z\setminus\{0\}\), with \(\gamma>0\) and \(\tau\geq1\). For every Gevrey index \(\mathfrak s>1+\tau\) and every sufficiently large coupling \(\lambda\), we construct a real-valued potential \(v_\lambda\in G^{\mathfrak s}(\T,\R)\) and a sequence of energies \(E_j\downarrow0\) such that \[ L_{v_\lambda}(0)\geq(1-\varepsilon_\lambda)\log\lambda, \qquad \sup_{j\geq1} L_{v_\lambda}(E_j)\leq(1-c_*)\log\lambda, \] where \(L_{v_\lambda}(E)\) denotes the Lyapunov exponent of the Schr\"odinger operator with potential \(\lambda v_\lambda\), \(c_*>0\) is an absolute constant, and \(\varepsilon_\lambda\to0\) as \(\lambda\to\infty\). For bounded-type frequencies (\(\tau=1\)), the regularity range \(\mathfrak s>2\) is sharp up to the endpoint \(\mathfrak s=2\), since the Lyapunov exponent is known to be continuous in energy for \(1<\mathfrak s<2\).

papers.title: Bistability with equal and independent removal in small bimolecular networks
papers.abstract: We classify two-species mass-action networks with at most three internal directed reactions on $\{X,Y,2X,X+Y,2Y\}$, positive inflows, and linear removal of both species. Among the 681 networks up to species exchange, exactly 27 admit two distinct positive hyperbolic attracting equilibria. The same 27 admit bistability with equal removal rates and with independently chosen positive removal rates. Each is minimal under reaction deletion. We give rational equal-removal witnesses for all positive cases and all-parameter exclusions for the remaining 654. The proof combines nullcline geometry, polynomial sign tests, resultant root bounds, and exact flux-cone decompositions. A separate rational-arithmetic implementation verifies the complete classification and its equilibrium certificates.

papers.title: Finiteness of Dziobek central configurations in the Newtonian five-body problem
papers.abstract: We prove that, for any five fixed strictly positive masses, the Newtonian central configurations of exact affine dimension three form finitely many similarity classes. The proof uses the Dziobek equations, two constant identities, and local analysis of zeros and poles on a compact complex curve.

papers.title: Large deviations and applications in homogeneous dynamics
papers.abstract: We consider the left translation action of an element $a$ on a finite-volume semisimple homogeneous space $G/\Gamma$, where $\operatorname{Ad}(a)$ is diagonalizable over $\mathbb{R}$. Assuming exponential mixing, we prove a sub-Gaussian large-deviation estimate for compactly supported smooth test functions. As an application, we prove effective uniqueness of the measure of maximal entropy. We also obtain quantitative pointwise equidistribution for Haar-almost every point on each full expanding horosphere.

papers.title: Pesin's entropy formula on attractors with continuous invariant splittings
papers.abstract: Under quantitative asymptotic hyperbolicity assumptions, we prove the existence of hyperbolic ergodic invariant probability measures satisfying Pesin's entropy formula for $C^1$ diffeomorphisms whose attractors admit extendable continuous invariant splittings. No dominated splitting is required on the attractor. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, the resulting measures are SRB measures. Our results apply to mostly expanding partially hyperbolic systems and to systems with strictly separated Lyapunov exponents under suitable statistical assumptions. We also construct examples with hyperbolic SRB measures of full support on attractors admitting no nontrivial dominated splitting, demonstrating the applicability of our criteria beyond results that require domination.

papers.title: The space of equators has infinite Hofer's diameter
papers.abstract: We settle several questions about Hofer's geometry of the two-sphere. We prove that the space of equators has infinite Hofer diameter, construct simple commutators of arbitrarily large Hofer norm, and exhibit a Hamiltonian diffeomorphism whose iterates escape to infinity in Hofer distance from the set of autonomous diffeomorphisms. Finally, we construct a bi-Lipschitz group monomorphism from the free group of rank two, equipped with its conjugation-invariant generator norm, into the Hamiltonian group equipped with Hofer's metric. The proof rests on an interplay between Lagrangian Floer theory in the fourth symmetric product of the sphere and combinatorial group theory. This paper was written with substantial assistance from AI.

papers.title: Amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations and applications to anti-treeability
papers.abstract: We study the structure of amenable subrelations of treeable measure-class-preserving equivalence relations, applying the Radon--Nikodym topography perspective initiated in our companion paper [TTD25]. For a nowhere smooth amenable subrelation, we show that the ends selected by each class in Adams's end selection theorem are precisely those which are nonvanishing along that class. From this, we derive a number of structure results about nowhere smooth amenable subrelations of treeable equivalence relations. For example, we show that every nowhere smooth amenable subrelation is contained in an essentially unique maximal amenable subrelation. This yields an anti-treeability criterion, which we use to show that every nonamenable locally compact second countable group with noncompact amenable radical is not treeable, and that every nonamenable nonunimodular treeable group has a compact open subgroup.

papers.title: Dynamics of a Harvested Predator-Prey Model with a Generalized Holling Type~III Response Capturing Group Defense
papers.abstract: We investigate a predator-prey model with constant prey harvesting and a generalized Holling type III functional response, focusing on the biological and dynamical consequences of allowing the parameter $b$ to be negative. In this regime, predation efficiency declines at high prey densities, potentially reflecting group defense. This change permits an additional coexistence equilibrium and introduces new bifurcation mechanisms affecting population persistence. We establish the existence of a codimension-three Bogdanov--Takens bifurcation, derive a codimension-three nilpotent-saddle unfolding, and investigate a codimension-two generalized Hopf bifurcation and the emergence of multiple limit cycles. Our analysis show that moderate harvesting weakens the protection conferred by high prey abundance; excessive harvesting leaves too few prey to sustain predator growth; and low harvesting preserves strong group defense, requiring high predator density for population persistence.

papers.title: Counting curves with bounded intersection
papers.abstract: This paper counts curves, and multicurves, on hyperbolic surfaces, providing explicit upper bounds that depend polynomially on length and exponentially in terms of an upper bound on self-intersection.

papers.title: Stochastic stability of master--slave synchronization for a class of PDEs with Burgers-type nonlinearity
papers.abstract: Master--slave synchronization reconstructs the evolving state of a reference (or master) system by continuously correcting a second system, the slave, using observations of the master. In applications, the observations are often contaminated by noise, so the corrections injected into the slave are themselves uncertain. In this paper we aim at quantifying the effect of noisy observations on master--slave synchronization for a family of evolution equations that combine a quadratic transport term with a polynomial linear differential operator. The family includes the Burgers, Kuramoto--Sivashinsky, Kawahara, Benney--Lin and Nikolaevskiy equations, among others. Under periodic boundary conditions, a Fourier--Galerkin approximation of order $K$ yields a finite-dimensional master--slave system in which white observation noise of intensity $\sigma$ is modeled through an It\^o stochastic differential equation. In this framework, we first establish local exponential stability of noiseless synchronization for sufficiently strong scalar coupling. Then we compare the stochastic synchronization error with its noiseless counterpart resulting from the same initial slave state, isolating in this way the effect of noise. Assuming bounded reference paths, the mean-square deviation between the noiseless and noisy synchronization errors is $\mathcal O(\sigma^2)$ on finite time intervals. Under additional regularity assumptions, we also bound the error between the finite-resolution stochastic slave model and the infinite-dimensional deterministic master field, explicitly separating spectral approximation error, deterministic synchronization error and observation noise. Numerical experiments for the Kawahara and Nikolaevskiy equations confirm the predicted noise scaling.

papers.title: Conditional Stable Laws and Rare-Event Limits for Absorbing Markov Chains
papers.abstract: We establish conditional limit theorems, pointwise in the initial state, for absorbing Markov chains on a compact metric space $M$. We assume $L^1(M,\rho)$-continuous transition densities, irreducibility and aperiodicity. For the observable $f_\beta(x)=d_M(x,x_0)^{-\beta}$, with suitable $x_0$ satisfying $\rho(B_r(x_0))\sim C_d(x_0)r^d$, we prove that the point-process of normalised observations converges to a Poisson random measure. This yields totally right-skewed $\alpha$-stable laws for $\alpha=d/\beta\in(0,2)$ and, at the boundary value $\alpha=2$, a Gaussian limit with the non-standard normalisation $\sqrt{n\log n}$. We also establish a conditional central limit theorem for $L^2$ observables, exponential deviation bounds for bounded observables and a conditional Poisson law for visits to shrinking targets. The results and remarks have been formalised in Lean~4.

papers.title: A dynamical approach towards Collatz conjecture
papers.abstract: The present work focuses on the study of the renowned Collatz conjecture, also known as the $3x+1$ problem. The analysis rests on the dynamics of an iterative map in binary form, defined on the dyadic rationals of $[1/2,\,1)$. We estimate how the length of the binary expansion of the iterated numbers changes, and we regard the iterative map as a perturbation of a circle map without periodic points, with an explicit bound for the error between both maps. A condition on the periods of periodic orbits is given; it is the classical argument of Crandall, and it recovers the lower bound of Eliahou for the length of nontrivial cycles. This version corrects several errors of the first one; they are listed in the Addendum.

papers.title: Simple Tilings of Riemannian Homogeneous Spaces
papers.abstract: We define simple tilings in the general context of a $G$-tiling on a Riemannian homogeneous space $M$ to be tilings by Riemannian simplices. As evidence that this definition is natural, we prove that a large class of tilings of $M$ are MLD to simple ones. We further show that there is an isomorphism between \u{C}ech cohomology and pattern-equivariant cohomology of simple tilings of homogeneous Riemannian Spaces. This demonstrates the utility of our definition by generalizing an established result on the topology of tiling spaces of Euclidean space.

papers.title: A direct proof of the existence of MME for finite horizon Sinai billiards
papers.abstract: The Sinai billiard map $T$ on the two-torus, i.e., the periodic Lorentz gas, is a discontinuous map. We provide two separate conditions for a finite horizon billiard to admit equilibrium states. The first one -- namely \emph{negligible singularities} -- only concerns the billiard table and implies upper semi-continuity for the metric pressure map of $T$. The condition of negligible singularities is shown to be generic (dense $G_\delta$) among billiard tables with $C^{3+\alpha}$ boundaries, in the $C^{3+\alpha}$ topology, and implies the sparse recurrence condition for the null potential. Compactness of the set of $T$-invariant measures is proved. For finite horizon Sinai billiards, we provide a bound on the defect of upper semi-continuity of the metric pressure map. From it, a condition of existence of equilibrium states only involving potentials is deduced. In both situations, for the potentials $g \equiv 0$ and $g = -h_{\rm top}(\Phi^1) \tau$, we recover and extend the recent results of the existence of measures of maximal entropy (MME) for both the map $T$ and the flow $\Phi^t$, due to Baladi and Demers for $T$, jointly with Carrand for $\Phi^t$. Upper semi-continuity of the metric entropy is shown. Assuming negligible singularities, equidistribution of the periodic orbits with respect to the unique MME is proved. A bound on the topological tail entropy is given.

papers.title: Singularity of the spectrum of typical minimal smooth area-preserving flows in any genus
papers.abstract: We consider smooth flows preserving a smooth invariant measure, or, equivalently, locally Hamiltonian flows on compact orientable surfaces, and show that almost every such locally Hamiltonian flow with only simple saddles has singular spectrum. Furthermore, we prove that for almost every pair of such flows, the elements of the pair are spectrally disjoint. More generally, the results from which these statements are deduced are singularity of the spectrum and pairwise spectral disjointness for special flows over full measure sets of interval exchange transformations under a roof with symmetric logarithmic singularities. Spectral singularity is proved using a criterion based on tightness of Birkhoff sums with exponential tail decay. The assumptions of the criterion are verified exploiting the cancellations proved by the last author to prove the absence of mixing in this class of flows, by showing that the latter can be combined with rigidity by exploiting the local product structure of Rauzy-Veech induction. Pairwise spectral disjointness then follows by producing mixing times (for the second flow), using a new mechanism for shearing based on what we call resonant rigidity times.

papers.title: Expansivity of algebraic semigroup actions
papers.abstract: For a semigroup $S$ and a right $\mathbb{Z}[S]$-submodule $J\leq \mathbb{Z}[S]^n$, we study expansivity of the algebraic action of $S$ induced on the Pontryagin dual of $\mathbb{Z}[S]^n/J$. We completely determine the class of semigroups for which expansivity of this action is characterized by the triviality of $J^\perp$, in terms of the existence of a finite subset $K\subseteq S$ such that $S=KS$. This condition is satisfied in particular by every monoid, and more generally by every semigroup with a left unital convolution Banach algebra, in which case we are able to extend the characterization of expansivity in terms of an invertibility condition when $J$ is finitely generated. We also exhibit examples of non-unital semigroups satisfying the hypotheses of our results.

papers.title: Exact dimensionality of stationary measures for random diffeomorphisms with all Lyapunov exponents equal and negative
papers.abstract:
We prove exact dimensionality of ergodic stationary measures for random compositions of $C^1$ diffeomorphisms of a closed manifold $M$ that contract at a single Lyapunov scale. More precisely, let $
u$ be a Borel probability measure on $\mathrm{Diff}^1(M)$ such that $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf}\|$ and $\log\sup_{x}\|{D_xf^{-1}}\|$ are $
u$-integrable, and let $\mu$ be an ergodic $
u$-stationary probability measure. If the top and bottom Lyapunov exponents of the derivative cocycle coincide and equal $\lambda<0$, then $\mu$ is exact dimensional and $\mathrm{dim}(\mu)=h_\mu^{\mathrm{F}}(
u)/(-\lambda)$, where $h_\mu^{\mathrm{F}}(
u)$ is the Furstenberg entropy.

papers.title: Khintchine dichotomy for images of self-similar measures and almost random walks
papers.abstract: Following the celebrated breakthrough in B\'enard-He-Zhang, we prove Khintchine dichotomy for push-forwards of self-similar measures on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under uniform $C^{1+\alpha}$ maps. For this, we also study almost random walks on $\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{R})/\mathrm{SL}(d+1,\mathbb{Z})$ and prove their effective equidistribution.
